newsitem.title: USA: Suits filed to block Sacramento, Calif., arena plan.
newsitem.headline: Suits filed to block Sacramento, Calif., arena plan.

text.p: Two lawsuits have been filed against the city of Sacramento over its plan to loan $70 million to the National Basketball Association's Sacramento Kings, according to a published report.

The loan, approved by the city council last month, would allow the basketball team's owners to restructure debt at Arco Arena, where the team plays, in exchange for an agreement to keep the team in Sacramento.
The Sacramento Bee reported Wednesday two lawsuits were filed against the loan plan by groups of taxpayers, including the so-called Sacramento City Taxpayers' Rights League.

Both lawsuits focus on the team's plan to impose a ticket surcharge for most events at Arco Arena. That money would be set aside in case it is needed to pay the team's loan debt to the city, according to the Bee.

The lawsuits allege that the Kings deal would violate California's Proposition 218, which strengthened existing state law to require that local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. Proposition 218 was approved by state voters last November.
The city of Sacramento plans to come to market in the coming weeks with notes, raising the money to refinance the arena and some of the team's debts, the city's treasurer said.
